title: Dependency calendar, signal-driven escalation, and canary windows
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: This ticket designs and delivers a calendar-driven dependency view with signal-based escalation rules and configurable canary windows for cross-team roadmap handoffs. The goal is to reduce blind handoffs between Eng/Design/Security/Infra by making date-bound commitments machine-readable, surfacing blocking signals (test regressions, infra capacity, security findings), and automating escalation + rollback windows. Deliverables: 1) a dependency calendar UI exportable to team calendars; 2) rule engine for signals (build failures, perf regressions, infra quotas, security triage age) and escalation actions (notify PM owners, open incident runbook, reserve burst capacity); 3) canary window templates tied to release lanes with automated fallthrough (rollforward/rollback) and a visible mitigation checklist. This is specific to roadmap handoffs where multiple teams must coordinate a release slice (e.g., runtime change + console feature + infra capacity). We will prioritize integration points with Console rollouts, Dedicated autoscaling policies, and the incident runbook library.
acceptance_criteria: Calendar view shows dependencies by owner and release lane and exports to iCal/Google calendar
Rule engine evaluates signals against thresholds and emits a prioritized alert to Slack/Console
Canary window templates can be attached to a deployment and execute automatic fallback when thresholds are exceeded
A lightweight runbook is created and linked when an escalation is triggered
Beta run with two cross-functional releases completed and retro notes captured
